summary: The study investigates the deposition of TaCxNy films using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) with tert-butylimido tri-diethylamido tantalum and methane/hydrogen reactive gas. The effect of methane concentration on film properties, such as resistivity and work function, is analyzed. The results show that methane concentration influences the phase composition, with lower resistivity and work function achieved at 1.5 mol% methane.
evidence: TaCxNy ﬁlm was deposited with plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition using tert-butylimido/H20851tri-diethylamido/H20852tantalum and methane/hydrogen reactive gas mixture. The resistivity was the lowest at 360 /H9262/H9024cm with 1.5 mol % methane due to the increase in the TaC conducting phase. The work function of the ﬁlm was measured from the metal-oxide-semiconductor structure with a slanted oxide layer. With the introduction of 1.5–2.5% methane, the TaC xNy ﬁlm with lower work function could be obtained.
